quotes.quote: A textual string may refer to two or more separate disease mentions. Such mentions are annotated with the **Composite Mention** category.

IF the head noun of a noun phrase denotes a pathological state or disorder, AND the phrase refers in context to a condition that an organism has or develops (even without a disease-marking word such as “disease” or “syndrome”), THEN label the full phrase as **Disease Class**.
- **Named diseases and attributive terms are not reclassified.** This rule uses **Disease Class** as a generic condition category.

note: Exclusion of the duration term 'slowly progressive' has no supporting text in Section 1.4.

quotes.quote: A textual string may refer to a disease name, but it may modify a noun phrase (or may not be a noun phrase itself). In such cases, annotate using the **Modifier** category.
quotes.condition_words: it may modify a noun phrase
quotes.cited_as: Section 3 (disease mention used as a modifier)

quotes.quote: - **Specific Disease**: Mentions that can be linked to one specific definition that does not include further categorization.
